desc: Parse input: N and the N×N character grid; build adjacency structures.
For each letter c (26), build in-list: for each vertex v, list of x with edge x→v labeled c; and out-list: for each vertex u, list of y with edge u→y labeled c.
Initialize dist[N][N] with -1; set dist[i][i]=0 and dist[i][j]=1 for each edge i→j; enqueue all these states in a deque (0-cost first, then 1-cost).
BFS: pop (u, v) with distance d; for each letter c, for each x in in-neighbors of u via c, for each y in out-neighbors of v via c, if dist[x][y] unset, set to d+2 and append to deque.
Verify BFS ordering correctness (states processed in nondecreasing distance since all edge weights are 2 and sources are 0/1; use a deque or simple queue with level discipline).
Output the dist matrix in the required format.

Write the complete Python solution: parse input, build in-edge lists and out-edge-by-letter lists, run the multi-source BFS over (u,v) state pairs with 0/1 sources and +2 transitions (with early exit when all states visited), and print the distance matrix.
